title: Police service looking for private funds
article: The Saskatoon Police Service is looking at the possibility of bolstering its budget through private funding as a way to finance various projects.

It doesn't mean renaming the downtown headquarters after a corporate sponsor, like Credit Union Centre for Cops, stitching a patch for Joe's Garage on the uniforms or repainting the cruisers with company logos.
Although, the $40 million would be nice, said chief Russell Sabo, referring to the deal the city received for renaming SaskPlace as Credit Union Centre.
"I suppose, for $40 million we could work something out," he joked.
It's more about finding donors who want to help out, as was done in 2001 with the kevlar vests for police dogs. A $10,000 donation from a local benefactor helped outfit half of the K-9 unit.

The anonymous benefactor stepped forward following the shooting death of Cyr, a five-year-old German shepherd member of the unit earlier that spring. That day, Cyr had accompanied his handler as police in their cruisers chased an armed suspect to the northern outskirts of the city.
An armed standoff ensued and Cyr was released to restrain the suspect, 33-year-old Keldon McMillan, who shot the dog with his .22 rifle. Police later shot and killed McMillan.
The police have also received donations that helped purchase bicycles for the force, Sabo noted.

A portion of the service's just-released strategic plan for 2006- 2010 focuses on managing financial resources. One objective is to "explore innovative and alternative methods to secure funding" through new partnerships with public and private agencies.

"We look at a lot of initiatives every year that would be great additions (to the force) but the question is, how do you fund that?" said Sabo. "There are times when we may have a civic minded group that might say, 'This makes sense for the community but if you can't do it on public dollars we can fund it.'
"Of course, it's always something that obviously has to be approved through the board (of police commissioners)."

Limited government funding in recent years has forced many public institutions to seek extra money elsewhere. The University of Saskatchewan has several partnerships and buildings renamed after corporate sponsors.

A $5-million donation from PotashCorp gave the U of S the extra funding it needed to revamp Griffiths Stadium in time to host the 2006 Vanier Cup. Consequently, the place is being given the new moniker of PotashCorp Park.
As for the police service, Sabo said the door is simply being left open to possibilities.

"We have to be very careful that we are not being seen as taking money and then being subject to some bias. We've got to make sure our integrity and ethics are not compromised by any kind of funding agreement we have," he said. "That's why public dollars going into policing, whether its federal dollars or provincial, is really the preferred method."
